text:
alex: quick heads-up — ran the autotuner sweep against gqa/mqa on the perf lab (ampere pool). seeing a consistent +7-12% token latency at seqlen=1024 when paged-kv blocksize=64. full run: 50k requests, 99th went from 290ms -> 320ms.

maria: ugh. did the CI alert pick this up or was this from bench runs?

alex: bench run. devops-bot flagged an integration perf regression yesterday: `perf/regress: inference-latency` on ampere-sm80. But i reproduced locally against master.

devops-bot: [automated] perf/regress: ampere-sm80: llm-infer@gqa-mqa - 99p +8.9% vs baseline. See: http://ci/perf/1955/report

maria: interesting — blocker could be kernel selection change in the autotuner scoring. i pushed a small tweak last week that favors paged kernels for MQA to reduce memory overhead. might be selecting a paged-kv kernel that has bad warp occupancy at these block sizes.

jon: logs? any kernel names? maybe the picker moved to `paged_kv_attn_v2_block64`? that one had known divergence on Ampere.

alex: yeah picker picked `paged_kv_attn_v2_block64` for several runs. i dumped the kernel metrics: occupancy drops ~15%, l2 load inefficiency up.

lina: quick thought: can we make the scoring function seqlen-aware? e.g. add a term that penalizes low occupancy at median_seq_len > 512. currently score = latency_est + alpha * mem_cost.

maria: agreed. propose: score = latency_est + alpha*mem_cost + beta*occupancy_penalty(seq_stats). For seqlen buckets >512, occupancy penalty weight should increase.

kevin: +1. we already have a `median_seq_len` metric emitted by router. could wire that into kernel picker as a feature. We should also fall back to contiguous-kv kernel when batch_size<=4 and seq>=1024 — those combos suffer on paged layout.

jon: quick repro command i've been using: `KVTUNE_BLOCKS=64 KVTUNE_LAYOUT=paged ./bench -m gqa-mqa -s 1024 -b 2 --profile-kernels > /tmp/run.log`

alex: dropping the paged kernel manually (force picker to contiguous) brought 99p down to 295ms in the same run (back to baseline). memory increased ~6% but still within dedicated pool.

maria: that signals kernel algorithmic mismatch rather than a model change. i can roll a patch to add seqlen-aware term. before we merge, can we quantify how often prod traffic hits the problematic combo? kevin, can you run a short trace over last 24h?

kevin: running now. short summary: 24h window, ampere-prod: ~3.8% of requests are (batch<=4, seq>=1024) for MQA; but they account for ~9% of 99p tail. pushing results to: http://perf/trace/1955/summary

lina: given that, short-term mitigation: add fallback rule in routing table: if seq>=1024 && batch<=4 && hardware.family==ampere then prefer contiguous-kv. longer-term: update autotuner features and re-run sweep including occupancy estimator.

jon: tests: when we bumped blocksize to 128 for paged kernel it recovered latency but memory access patterns got worse on smaller batches — fragmentation and longer memcpy times. so 128 is a stopgap.

alex: proposed action items:
- maria: PR to add median_seq_len and occupancy penalty to kernel scoring (small change)
- kevin: run A/B where picker uses new score vs old for 10% traffic on ampere (duration 6h)
- lina: add routing fallback rule as emergency switch
- jon: add a kernel bench that sweeps blocksize 32/64/128 and emits occupancy+L2 stats per kernel/hw

maria: i'll open PR by EOD with unit tests. scoring patch will be gated behind feature flag `kernel_score_seqaware`.

kevin: started A/B job: `./ab_test --exp kernel_score_seqaware --pct 10 --hw ampere --dur 6h`

devops-bot: [automated] job/1955-ab started. link: http://ci/ab/1955

alex: quick note — if A/B shows improvement, we should still keep fallback for 24h while rolling. avoid flip flop. :thumbsup:

jon: also adding a small profiler hook to record `blocksize -> occupancy` heatmap per model-version. can help autotuner learning.

lina: filing internal incident ticket to track rollout + rollback plan: RD-ISSUE-3245. tagging infra/sre for visibility.

maria: thanks all — i'll post PR link once ready. will include benchmark matrix and a small script to reproduce with `KVTUNE_*` envs.

alex: perfect. if anyone wants the raw logs i uploaded run.log to /nfs/perf/1955/*.zip.

kevin: after A/B finishes i'll share latency deltas and allocation graphs.

lina: thanks team. small wins here reduce tail for a lot of customers.

maria: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/kernel-picker/pulls/812 (draft). please review. :eyes:

alex: reviewing now.

jon: will add bench harness changes in a follow-up PR.

(END)
